lesson.title: Setting the Stage for the Cold War and Decolonization
lesson.summary: How World War II left two superpowers, exhausted colonial empires, and new demands for independence.
learningGoals: Explain the historical context of the Cold War after 1945.
lesson.bigIdea: World War II weakened Europe's empires and left the United States and the Soviet Union as rivals, setting the stage for both the Cold War and decolonization.
lesson.context: In 1945 the victors had defeated fascism, but they disagreed about what kind of world should replace the one the war destroyed.

sections.title: A world with two superpowers

blocks.text: The war left Europe and East Asia in ruins. The United States produced about half of the world's manufactured goods in 1945 and alone had the atomic bomb. The Soviet Union had lost about 27 million people, but its armies occupied Eastern Europe.

The two powers had allied only to defeat Germany. The United States favored capitalism and elected governments; the Soviet Union, a one-party communist state, wanted friendly governments on its borders to protect against another invasion.

In 1945, fifty nations founded the United Nations to keep the peace. Its Security Council gave the United States, the Soviet Union, Britain, France, and China permanent seats and the power to veto decisions.

blocks.title: Cause and effect
blocks.text: The defeat of Germany and Japan removed the common enemy, and the two strongest survivors had opposing political and economic systems.

sections.takeaway: World War II left the United States and the Soviet Union dominant, with opposing systems and goals.

sections.title: Empires under pressure

blocks.text: Britain and France won the war but were deeply in debt. Japan's rapid conquest of European colonies in Southeast Asia in 1941 and 1942 had shown that colonial rulers could be beaten.

Millions of colonial subjects had fought for the Allies. In the Atlantic Charter of 1941, Britain and the United States endorsed self-determination, the right of peoples to choose their own government. Nationalists demanded that the principle apply to them, and decolonization, the end of colonial rule, began within two years of the war's end.

blocks.title: Common trap
blocks.text: Decolonization was not a gift from weakened empires. Colonial peoples organized, protested, and sometimes fought for independence; war only made their demands harder to refuse.

sections.takeaway: World War II drained the colonial powers and strengthened nationalist movements.

connections.title: From world war to Cold War
connections.body: Unit 7 ended with the superpowers emerging from World War II. Unit 8 follows their rivalry and the end of the empires the war had weakened.
